docs.title: Internet Topology Pipeline
docs.text:
Reconstruct the Internet's AS-level topology from publicly available BGP routing data published by RIPE NCC's Routing Information Service (RIS) and RouteViews.

The pipeline downloads MRT RIB snapshot files from route collectors, extracts AS paths, and produces a deduplicated edge list where each line is a pair of ASNs observed to be directly connected:

00001299 00003356
00001299 00022773
00003356 00015169

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
BGP routers exchange reachability information as AS paths — ordered sequences of Autonomous System Numbers (ASNs) that a route traverses. The path 1299 3356 15169 means links exist between AS 1299↔3356 and AS 3356↔15169.

RIPE RIS operates a global network of route collectors (rrc00–rrc25), each peering with many BGP routers. Periodically, each collector dumps a full snapshot of its routing table into an MRT-format binary file. This pipeline processes those snapshots to reconstruct the observed AS-level topology.

RouteViews provides additional vantage points across ~40 collectors worldwide, processed identically to RIS data.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Tool Purpose Install Python 3.12+ Runtime uv manages this uv Python package manager curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh \| sh just Pipeline orchestration cargo install just or system package bgpreader MRT file parser Part of BGPStream; install via system package bash 4+ Required for collect.sh macOS: brew install bash

macOS bash

macOS ships with bash 3.2. The collect.sh fleet script requires bash 4+ for export -f. Install a newer version with brew install bash. This is only needed on the central machine that runs collect; remote nodes only need ssh and rsync.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/carlos-cagnazzo/internet-topology-ris
cd internet-topology-ris
uv sync

Verify bgpreader is available:

bgpreader --version

docs.title: Pipeline at a Glance
docs.text:
get-mrt.py          ──┐
                       ├──▶  extract-paths.py  ──▶  build-topology.py
get-routeviews.py   ──┘
  1. Download — fetch 00:00 UTC RIB snapshots (.gz from RIS, .bz2 from RouteViews)
  2. Extract — run bgpreader on each file, write per-file AS path lists
  3. Build — read all path files, extract edges, deduplicate, write topology

See Quick Start to run it, or Pipeline for a deep dive.

docs.title: Fleet Workflow
docs.text: Processing a full day of data (all RIS collectors + RouteViews) can take several hours on a single machine. The fleet workflow distributes the download and extraction steps across multiple machines, then merges the results centrally.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Node A: just date=YYYYMMDD collectors=rrc00-rrc08 slice
Node B: just date=YYYYMMDD collectors=rrc09-rrc17 slice
Node C: just date=YYYYMMDD collectors=rrc18-rrc25 slice

Central: just date=YYYYMMDD collect
Central: just date=YYYYMMDD topology

The slice recipe runs download + process only — no topology is built on the node. Path files are named after their collector, so all nodes write into the same destination directory without conflicts when collected centrally.

Optionally, you can also run just date=YYYYMMDD topology on each node to inspect a partial topology while the central collection is pending.

docs.title: 1. Create fleet.csv
docs.text:
Copy the example and fill in your machines:

cp fleet.csv.example fleet.csv

Format: username,hostname,/absolute/path/to/repo — one machine per line. Lines starting with # are ignored.

# username,hostname,repo_path
carlos,node1.example.com,/home/carlos/src/internet-topology-ris
carlos,node2.example.com,/home/carlos/src/internet-topology-ris
carlos,mac.local,/Users/carlos/src/internet-topology-ris

fleet.csv is gitignored — it contains hostnames and paths specific to your deployment. The fleet.csv.example template is tracked.

docs.title: 2. Ensure SSH access
docs.text:
All machines in fleet.csv must be reachable with a shared SSH key from the central machine. Test with:

ssh carlos@node1.example.com "echo ok"

docs.title: 3. Clone the repo on each node
docs.text:
Each node needs the repo cloned at the path listed in fleet.csv:

git clone https://github.com/carlos-cagnazzo/internet-topology-ris \
  /home/carlos/src/internet-topology-ris

docs.title: Running a slice
docs.text:
On each node, assign a collector range and run slice:

just date=20260101 collectors=rrc00-rrc08 slice

For RouteViews, you can split manually by passing specific collectors to get-routeviews.py directly — the download-routeviews recipe runs all 12 default collectors as a unit.

docs.title: Collecting path files
docs.text:
Once all nodes have finished their slices, collect the path files from the central machine:

just date=20260101 collect

This runs collect.sh, which rsyncs each node's paths/20260101/ directory into the local ./paths/20260101/. Up to jobs rsyncs run in parallel (default 2):

just date=20260101 jobs=4 collect

Per-host logs go to ./logs/collect-20260101/<hostname>.log. Any failed hosts are reported at the end; the exit code is non-zero if any rsync failed.

docs.title: Building the global topology
docs.text:
After collecting, build the topology from all merged path files:

just date=20260101 topology

docs.title: Fetching output files from remote machines
docs.text:
fetch-results.sh collects output files (topologies) rather than path files, using rsync into per-host subdirectories to avoid conflicts:

./fetch-results.sh

Configure SOURCES, INCLUDES, and EXCLUDE at the top of the script. Count unique ASNs across all fetched topologies:

zcat fetch/*/topology-????????.txt \
  | awk '{print $1; print $2}' \
  | sort -un \
  | wc -l

Legacy

fetch-results.sh predates the fleet/collect workflow and may be superseded by it for most use cases. It remains useful for ad-hoc collection without a fleet.csv.

docs.title: Typical three-date workflow across a fleet
docs.text:
# On each node (different collector slice per node):
for d in 20260101 20260201 20260301; do
  just date=$d collectors=rrc00-rrc08 slice
done

# On the central machine:
for d in 20260101 20260201 20260301; do
  just date=$d jobs=4 collect
  just date=$d topology
done

docs.title: Single machine, one date
docs.text:
The simplest way to run the full pipeline — downloads from all RIS collectors plus the default RouteViews subset, extracts paths, and builds combined + IPv4 + IPv6 topologies.

just date=20260101 collectors=rrc00-rrc25 pipeline

Variable order

just requires variable assignments before the recipe name: just date=20260101 pipeline ✓ just pipeline date=20260101 ✗

Output lands in ./output/20260101/:

output/20260101/
  topology-20260101.txt        # all-AF edge list
  topology-20260101-asns.txt   # unique ASN list
  topology-20260101-v4.txt     # IPv4 edge list
  topology-20260101-v4-asns.txt
  topology-20260101-v6.txt     # IPv6 edge list
  topology-20260101-v6-asns.txt

Each edge list line is a pair of zero-padded ASNs, sorted numerically within the pair and across all lines:

00000006 00022773
00001299 00003356
00001299 00022773

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
Run steps individually when you need to reprocess or debug:

# 1. Download RIS snapshots
just date=20260101 collectors=rrc00-rrc25 download

# 2. Download RouteViews snapshots
just date=20260101 download-routeviews

# 3. Extract AS paths from all downloaded files
just date=20260101 process

# 4. Build topology (combined + v4 + v6)
just date=20260101 topology

Or build only one address family:

just date=20260101 topology-v4

docs.title: Three dates, multiple collectors
docs.text:
for d in 20260101 20260201 20260301; do
  just date=$d collectors=rrc00-rrc25 pipeline
done

docs.text:

docs.title: RIS Collectors
docs.text:
RIPE RIS operates collectors rrc00 through rrc25. Use rrc00-rrc25 in --collectors to include all of them.

Collector Location rrc00 Amsterdam, NL rrc01 London, UK rrc03 Amsterdam, NL rrc04 Geneva, CH rrc05 Vienna, AT rrc06 Otemachi, JP rrc07 Stockholm, SE rrc10 Milan, IT rrc11 New York, US rrc12 Frankfurt, DE rrc13 Moscow, RU rrc14 Palo Alto, US rrc15 São Paulo, BR rrc16 Miami, US rrc18 Barcelona, ES rrc19 Johannesburg, ZA rrc20 Zurich, CH rrc21 Paris, FR rrc22 Bucharest, RO rrc23 Singapore, SG rrc24 Montevideo, UY rrc25 Amsterdam, NL

docs.title: RouteViews Collectors (default set)
docs.text:
The download-routeviews recipe uses a working subset of ~40 available collectors. Full index: https://www.routeviews.org/routeviews/index.php/collectors/

Collector ID Region route-views.amsix Europe (AMS-IX) namex.fco Europe (Rome) hkix.hkg Asia (Hong Kong) route-views.sg Asia (Singapore) route-views.chicago North America route-views2 North America pacwave.lax North America crix.sjo North America ix-br2.gru Latin America (São Paulo) route-views.rio Latin America (Rio) route-views.kixp Africa (Nairobi) route-views.perth Oceania

docs.title: Edge list (topology.txt)
docs.text:
One undirected edge per line. Both ASNs are plain integers (or zero-padded to 8 digits with --justify-output). The smaller ASN always appears first. Lines are sorted numerically by the first ASN, then the second.

6 22773
1299 3356
1299 22773

With --justify-output:

00000006 00022773
00001299 00003356
00001299 00022773

docs.title: ASN list (topology-asns.txt)
docs.text: One ASN per line, sorted numerically. Zero-padded if --justify-output was used.

docs.title: Path list (topology-paths.txt)
docs.text: One AS path per line (space-separated ASNs), sorted numerically by leading ASN. Written only when --paths is passed to build-topology.py.

docs.title: Annotated topology (topology-annotated.txt)
docs.text: Six columns per line: ASN1 ASN2 CC1 RIR1 CC2 RIR2. Country codes are lowercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. RIR names: arin, ripencc, apnic, lacnic, afrinic. Absent ASNs annotated as unknown unknown.

docs.title: NRO Delegated Stats
docs.text:
Used by --filter-registered in build-topology.py and by the geo-filter.py and annotate-topology.py graph analysis tools.

URL Latest https://ftp.ripe.net/pub/stats/ripencc/nro-stats/latest/nro-delegated-stats Historical https://ftp.ripe.net/pub/stats/ripencc/nro-stats/YYYYMMDD/nro-delegated-stats

Relevant statuses: assigned (keep), available / reserved (discard).

docs.title: bgpreader
docs.text:
bgpreader is the system binary used by extract-paths.py to parse MRT files. It handles both .gz and .bz2 inputs transparently.

Output is |-delimited. Relevant columns (0-indexed):

Column Field 1 Element type (R = RIB entry, B = block start — skip B lines) 9 Prefix (colon present → IPv6) 11 AS path

Only R lines are processed. The option to read a single file is rib-file:

bgpreader -d singlefile -o rib-file=<path>

docs.title: .gitignore summary
docs.text:
The following are gitignored and must not be committed:

Path Reason mrt/ Downloaded MRT files (large binary data) paths/ Extracted AS path files (large) topology*.txt Generated output files nro-delegated-stats* Cached NRO stats fleet.csv Deployment-specific; copy from fleet.csv.example fetch/ Rsync staging from fetch-results.sh output/ (not gitignored by default — add if needed)

docs.title: Graph Analysis
docs.text: The graph-analysis/ directory contains tools for analysing and transforming topology files. All run via uv run graph-analysis/<tool> from the repo root.

docs.title: Tools at a glance
docs.text:
Tool Input Output Purpose topology-to-gml.py .txt edge list .gml Convert to GML for Gephi/yEd gml-to-topology.py .gml .txt edge list Convert GML back to edge list topology-core.py .txt edge list .txt edge list Filter to high-degree nodes geo-filter.py .txt or .gml .txt + .gml Filter to one or more countries hubs.py .txt or .gml .txt hub list List high-degree ASNs annotate-topology.py .txt edge list .txt with CC+RIR Add country/RIR columns asn-presence.py *-asns-YYYYMMDD.txt files matrix .txt Day-by-day ASN presence matrix

Also available at the repo root:

Tool Purpose topology-ops.py Set operations (union / difference) on topology files lookup-as.py Look up ASN holder info via RIPEstat

docs.title: Reduce before visualising
docs.text:
Large topologies (200k+ edges) are slow to render in Gephi. Filter to a core first:

# Keep only nodes with degree ≥ 10
uv run graph-analysis/topology-core.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --output output/20260101/topology-core10.txt \
  --min-degree 10

# Convert core to GML with enriched labels
uv run graph-analysis/topology-to-gml.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-core10.txt \
  --enrich --min-degree 10

docs.title: Regional analysis
docs.text:
# Latin America topology
uv run graph-analysis/geo-filter.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --countries ar,br,cl,co,mx,pe,uy,ve \
  --output output/20260101/latam

# Annotate with country/RIR for further analysis
uv run graph-analysis/annotate-topology.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --date 20260101

docs.title: Track ASN stability over time
docs.text:
# Build topologies for several dates, then build the presence matrix
uv run graph-analysis/asn-presence.py \
  --input "output/*/topology-*-asns.txt" \
  --output output/asn-presence.txt

docs.title: hubs.py
docs.text:
Lists ASNs with degree ≥ --min-degree from a topology edge list or GML file. Degree is computed in a single pass for .txt input — no GML conversion required.

uv run graph-analysis/hubs.py --input <file> --min-degree <N> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt/.txt.gz) or .gml --output input stem + -hubs.txt Output file --min-degree required Minimum degree threshold --wide off Two-column output (ASN degree), sorted by degree descending

Without --wide: one ASN per line, sorted numerically. With --wide: two columns sorted by degree descending — useful for ranking.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# List all ASNs with degree ≥ 100
uv run graph-analysis/hubs.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --min-degree 100

# Ranked by degree
uv run graph-analysis/hubs.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --min-degree 50 --wide

docs.title: annotate-topology.py
docs.text:
Enriches a topology edge list by appending four columns to each edge: cc1 rir1 cc2 rir2 — the country code and RIR for each ASN, sourced from the NRO delegated stats.

uv run graph-analysis/annotate-topology.py --input <file> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt or .txt.gz) --output input stem + -annotated.txt Output file --date latest NRO stats snapshot date YYYYMMDD --justify-output off Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

Country codes are lowercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. RIR names: arin, ripencc, apnic, lacnic, afrinic. ASNs absent from the NRO file are annotated as unknown unknown.

Input sort order is preserved.

docs.title: Output format
docs.text:
6057 3359 uy lacnic us arin
174 1916 us arin br lacnic
64512 65001 unknown unknown unknown unknown

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Annotate with the NRO snapshot matching the topology date
uv run graph-analysis/annotate-topology.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --date 20260101

# With zero-padding
uv run graph-analysis/annotate-topology.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --output output/20260101/topology-20260101-annotated.txt \
  --date 20260101 --justify-output

docs.title: asn-presence.py
docs.text:
Builds a day-by-day ASN presence matrix from {stem}-asns-YYYYMMDD.txt files produced by build-topology.py. One row per unique ASN, one column per date, values 0/1.

uv run graph-analysis/asn-presence.py --input <glob> [--output <file>]
Flag Default Description --input required Glob matching *-asns-YYYYMMDD.txt files. Repeat for multiple globs. --output first matched file's directory / asn-presence.txt Output matrix file

The first line is a header: ASN YYYYMMDD YYYYMMDD …. ASNs are zero-padded to 8 digits.

Load in pandas:

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("asn-presence.txt", sep=r"\s+", index_col=0, dtype=int)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
uv run graph-analysis/asn-presence.py \
  --input "output/*/topology-*-asns.txt" \
  --output output/asn-presence.txt

docs.title: topology-ops.py
docs.text:
Set operations on two or more topology edge list files. Both plain (6 22773) and zero-padded (00000006 00022773) formats are handled; comparison is always numeric.

uv run topology-ops.py --op <add|sub> --output <file> [--justify-output] FILE [FILE ...]
Argument Description FILE ... Two or more topology edge list files (positional) --op add Union — all edges present in any input file, deduplicated --op sub Difference — edges in the first file not present in any remaining file --output Output file --justify-output Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Merge three dates
uv run topology-ops.py --op add \
  --output output/combined.txt --justify-output \
  output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  output/20260201/topology-20260201.txt \
  output/20260301/topology-20260301.txt

# Links present in January but gone by March
uv run topology-ops.py --op sub \
  --output output/disappeared.txt \
  output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  output/20260301/topology-20260301.txt

docs.title: lookup-as.py
docs.text:
Queries the RIPEstat Data API for one or more ASNs. Returns AS holder name, announced prefix count, last-seen timestamp, and announced status.

uv run lookup-as.py --asn <N>
uv run lookup-as.py --file <file>
cat asns.txt | uv run lookup-as.py
Flag Default Description --asn — Single ASN to look up --file — File with one ASN per line; - for stdin --output — Write results as TSV alongside terminal output --concurrency 10 Max parallel API requests (batch mode)

Batch mode shows a live progress bar. Results are displayed as a rich table.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Single ASN
uv run lookup-as.py --asn 15169

# Batch from the dropped-ASNs list
uv run lookup-as.py \
  --file output/20260101/topology-20260101-dropped-asns.txt \
  --output output/20260101/dropped-asns-info.tsv

# Pipe the hub list
uv run graph-analysis/hubs.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --min-degree 100 | uv run lookup-as.py

docs.title: Conversion Tools
docs.text: Tools for converting between topology edge list format and GML.

docs.title: topology-to-gml.py
docs.text:
Converts a topology edge list (.txt) to a GML file for import into Gephi, yEd, Cytoscape, or any graph tool that reads GML.

uv run graph-analysis/topology-to-gml.py --input <file> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt or .txt.gz) --output input with .gml extension Output GML file --min-degree 3 Filter: only include edges where both endpoints have degree ≥ N --enrich off Fetch AS holder names from RIPEstat and use as node labels --enrich-min-degree 3 Only enrich nodes with degree ≥ N (cheaper than enriching all nodes)

When --enrich is active, holder names are fetched from the RIPEstat API and cached at ~/.cache/internet-topology-ris/as-names.json with a 60-day TTL. Nodes below --enrich-min-degree keep their ASN as label.

To produce a filtered edge list (.txt) rather than a GML, use topology-core.py instead.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Basic conversion, no filtering
uv run graph-analysis/topology-to-gml.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt

# Filter to core (degree ≥ 5) + enrich labels for well-connected nodes
uv run graph-analysis/topology-to-gml.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --output output/20260101/topology-core5.gml \
  --min-degree 5 \
  --enrich --enrich-min-degree 20

docs.title: gml-to-topology.py
docs.text:
Inverse of topology-to-gml.py. Reads a GML file and writes a two-column topology edge list. Useful for round-tripping through Gephi (e.g. after manual layout or community detection).

uv run graph-analysis/gml-to-topology.py --input <file> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required GML file --output input with .txt extension Output edge list --min-degree (none) Optional: filter to edges where both endpoints have degree ≥ N --justify-output off Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

ASNs are always read from the node asn attribute (safe for enriched GML files that carry string labels).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Round-trip: convert back from Gephi export
uv run graph-analysis/gml-to-topology.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-gephi.gml \
  --output output/20260101/topology-gephi.txt

# With degree filter
uv run graph-analysis/gml-to-topology.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology.gml \
  --min-degree 10 \
  --justify-output

docs.title: topology-core.py
docs.text:
Filters a topology edge list to edges where both endpoints have degree ≥ --min-degree. Produces a valid topology file in the same two-column format.

Useful before visualisation (large topologies are slow in Gephi) or before analysis steps you want to run only on well-connected ASNs.

uv run graph-analysis/topology-core.py --input <file> --min-degree <N> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt or .txt.gz) --output input stem + -core.txt Output filtered edge list --min-degree required Minimum degree (both endpoints must qualify) --wide off Add DEG1 DEG2 columns to the output --justify-output off Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

Degree is computed from the input file directly — no GML conversion required.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Keep only edges where both ASNs have degree ≥ 10
uv run graph-analysis/topology-core.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --min-degree 10

# Same, but annotate with degrees and zero-pad
uv run graph-analysis/topology-core.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --output output/20260101/topology-core10.txt \
  --min-degree 10 --wide --justify-output

docs.title: geo-filter.py
docs.text:
Filters a topology to edges where both ASNs are assigned to one of the given ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, according to the NRO delegated stats. ASNs absent from the NRO file are excluded.

Always produces two output files:

  • {output}.txt — filtered edge list
  • {output}.gml — filtered graph with a country node attribute
uv run graph-analysis/geo-filter.py --input <file> --countries <cc,...> [OPTIONS]
Flag Default Description --input required Topology edge list (.txt/.txt.gz) or .gml --countries required Comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (lowercase) --output input stem + -geo Base output path (no extension — both .txt and .gml written) --date latest NRO stats snapshot date YYYYMMDD for reproducible filtering --justify-output off Zero-pad ASNs to 8 digits

NRO stats are fetched and cached next to the input file.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Latin American topology
uv run graph-analysis/geo-filter.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --countries ar,br,cl,co,mx,pe,uy,ve \
  --output output/20260101/latam \
  --date 20260101

# Single country
uv run graph-analysis/geo-filter.py \
  --input output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --countries br \
  --output output/20260101/brazil

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
The pipeline is a linear three-step process orchestrated by just.

get-mrt.py          ──┐
                       ├──▶  extract-paths.py  ──▶  build-topology.py
get-routeviews.py   ──┘

./mrt/<date>/       ──▶  ./paths/<date>/       ──▶  ./output/<date>/
  *.gz (RIS)              *.gz.txt
  *.bz2 (RouteViews)      *.gz.v4.txt
                          *.gz.v6.txt
                          *.bz2.txt
                          *.bz2.v4.txt
                          *.bz2.v6.txt

docs.title: Justfile recipes
docs.text: Recipe What it runs pipeline download + download-routeviews + process + topology download get-mrt.py for the given collectors download-routeviews get-routeviews.py for the default RouteViews subset process extract-paths.py on all .gz and .bz2 files topology topology-combined + topology-v4 + topology-v6 topology-combined build-topology.py on combined path files topology-v4 build-topology.py on IPv4 path files topology-v6 build-topology.py on IPv6 path files slice download + process only (for fleet nodes) collect rsync path files from all fleet nodes pack-and-publish tar + copy to a publish point

docs.title: Justfile variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description date (empty) Snapshot date YYYYMMDD. Required for download and topology. collectors rrc00 RIS collector spec — individual, list, or range (e.g. rrc00-rrc25). mrt_dir ./mrt Root for downloaded MRT files. Date subdir created automatically. paths_dir ./paths Root for extracted path files. Date subdir created automatically. output_dir ./output Root for topology output. Date subdir created automatically. output topology-<date>.txt Combined output filename. output_v4 topology-<date>-v4.txt IPv4 output filename. output_v6 topology-<date>-v6.txt IPv6 output filename. jobs 2 Parallel rsync jobs for collect. pubpoint /var/www/html/topo Destination for pack-and-publish.

docs.title: Pages in this section
docs.text:
• Download — get-mrt.py and get-routeviews.py
  • Extract Paths — extract-paths.py
  • Build Topology — build-topology.py

docs.title: Download
docs.text: Two scripts handle downloading, one per data source. Both follow the same interface and produce files in the same output directory; extract-paths.py handles both transparently.

docs.title: get-mrt.py — RIPE RIS
docs.text:
Downloads the 00:00 UTC RIB snapshot (bview) for a given date from one or more RIS collectors. Already-downloaded files are skipped. Failed transfers are reported per-collector and counted in the summary without aborting the run.

uv run get-mrt.py --collectors <spec> --date <YYYYMMDD> [--output-dir <dir>]
Flag Required Description --collectors yes Collector specification (see below) --date yes Snapshot date in YYYYMMDD format --output-dir no Output directory. Default: ./mrt

Output filenames: bview.rrcXX.YYYYMMDD.0000.gz

docs.title: Collector specification
docs.text:
--collectors accepts a comma-separated mix of individual names and ranges:

Syntax Example Expands to Individual rrc00 rrc00 List rrc00,rrc04,rrc11 rrc00, rrc04, rrc11 Range rrc00-rrc05 rrc00 through rrc05 Mixed rrc00-rrc03,rrc11 rrc00–rrc03, rrc11

RIS has collectors rrc00 through rrc25. Use rrc00-rrc25 to collect from all of them.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# All collectors
just date=20260101 collectors=rrc00-rrc25 download

# Single collector
uv run get-mrt.py --collectors rrc00 --date 20260101

# Mixed specification
uv run get-mrt.py --collectors rrc00-rrc05,rrc11,rrc23 --date 20260101 --output-dir ./mrt/20260101

docs.title: get-routeviews.py — RouteViews
docs.text:
Same interface as get-mrt.py but targets the RouteViews archive. Output files are .bz2 format.

uv run get-routeviews.py --collectors <list> --date <YYYYMMDD> [--output-dir <dir>]
Flag Required Description --collectors yes Comma-separated RouteViews collector IDs --date yes Snapshot date in YYYYMMDD format --output-dir no Output directory. Default: ./mrt

Output filenames: rib.<collector>.YYYYMMDD.0000.bz2

RouteViews collectors do not follow a numeric sequence, so range notation is not supported — use a comma-separated list.

docs.title: Default collector set
docs.text:
The download-routeviews justfile recipe uses a working subset of the ~40 available collectors:

Collector ID Region route-views.amsix Europe (AMS-IX) namex.fco Europe (Rome) hkix.hkg Asia (Hong Kong) route-views.sg Asia (Singapore) route-views.chicago North America route-views2 North America pacwave.lax North America crix.sjo North America ix-br2.gru Latin America (São Paulo) route-views.rio Latin America (Rio) route-views.kixp Africa (Nairobi) route-views.perth Oceania

To add more, extend the --collectors argument in the download-routeviews recipe in the justfile. Full collector index: https://www.routeviews.org/routeviews/index.php/collectors/

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Default subset via justfile
just date=20260101 download-routeviews

# Custom selection
uv run get-routeviews.py \
  --collectors route-views.amsix,route-views2,route-views.sg \
  --date 20260101 \
  --output-dir ./mrt/20260101

docs.title: Downloading a full month of RouteViews data
docs.text:
download-routeviews-month.sh downloads one bview per day for an entire month, running up to N days in parallel:

./download-routeviews-month.sh YYYYMM [parallel_jobs]

# Download all of January 2026, 4 days in parallel
./download-routeviews-month.sh 202601 4

Output: ./mrt-routeviews/YYYYMMDD/ Logs: ./logs/routeviews-YYYYMM/YYYYMMDD.log

docs.title: Extract Paths
docs.text:
extract-paths.py calls bgpreader on each MRT file and writes three sidecar files per input — one combined, one IPv4-only, one IPv6-only. A file set is skipped only if all three outputs already exist.

uv run extract-paths.py --input-files <glob> [--output-dir <dir>]
Flag Required Description --input-files yes Glob pattern matching MRT files (.gz or .bz2) --output-dir no Output directory. Default: ./paths

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
The output filename is the full input filename (including the .gz/.bz2 extension) with an additional suffix appended:

Suffix Contents .gz.txt / .bz2.txt All paths (combined IPv4 + IPv6) .gz.v4.txt / .bz2.v4.txt IPv4-only paths .gz.v6.txt / .bz2.v6.txt IPv6-only paths

Address family is detected from the prefix field (column 9 in bgpreader output): a colon (:) in the prefix indicates IPv6.

Output files are gzip-compressed despite the .txt extension. build-topology.py detects this automatically via magic bytes.

docs.title: Path cleaning rules
docs.text:
Applied before writing each path:

  • Prepend removal — consecutive duplicate ASNs are collapsed: 64500 64500 64501 → 64500 64501
  • AS set truncation — paths containing AS sets (e.g. {64500,64501}) are truncated at that point; edges before the set are kept

docs.title: Justfile
docs.text:
The process recipe runs twice — once for .gz files (RIS) and once for .bz2 files (RouteViews):

just date=20260101 process

If no files match a glob, the invocation prints a notice and exits cleanly (not an error).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Process all RIS files for a date
uv run extract-paths.py \
  --input-files "./mrt/20260101/*.gz" \
  --output-dir ./paths/20260101

# Process all RouteViews files for the same date
uv run extract-paths.py \
  --input-files "./mrt/20260101/*.bz2" \
  --output-dir ./paths/20260101

docs.title: Build Topology
docs.text:
build-topology.py reads AS path files, extracts edges, deduplicates, and writes the topology. It accepts multiple --input globs and merges RIS and RouteViews files seamlessly. Workers process files in parallel.

uv run build-topology.py --input <glob> [--input <glob> ...] [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Flags
docs.text: Flag Default Description --input required Glob matching path .txt files. Repeat to add more patterns. --output ./topology.txt Output file for the edge list. --date (none) Snapshot date YYYYMMDD. Required when using --filter-registered with a historical NRO snapshot. --filter-registered off Exclude paths containing any non-assigned ASN (see below). --justify-output off Zero-pad all ASNs to 8 digits in all output files. --paths off Also write a deduplicated path list (large; off by default). --workers cpu_count Number of parallel worker processes.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
All files are written to the same directory as --output, named after its stem.

File Description {stem}.txt Deduplicated undirected edge list. One AS1 AS2 per line, AS1 < AS2, sorted numerically. {stem}-asns.txt Sorted list of all unique ASNs in the topology. {stem}-paths.txt (only with --paths) Deduplicated AS paths, sorted numerically by leading ASN. {stem}-dropped-asns.txt (only with --filter-registered) ASNs excluded because they are not assigned in the NRO stats.

docs.title: --filter-registered
docs.text:
Filters at the path level: a path is excluded entirely if any of its ASNs is not assigned in the NRO delegated extended stats. This removes paths transiting unallocated, reserved, or private ASNs.

The NRO stats file is cached next to the input path files:

  • Historical (when --date is provided): nro-delegated-stats-YYYYMMDD — fetched once and cached permanently (the historical file never changes).
  • Latest (no --date): nro-delegated-stats — re-downloaded if older than 24 hours.

docs.title: --justify-output
docs.text:
Zero-pads all ASN numbers to 8 digits in every output file, making them fixed-width:

# Without --justify-output   # With --justify-output
6 22773                       00000006 00022773
1299 3356                     00001299 00003356

Fixed-width output is useful for lexicographic sorting tools and for consistent alignment in downstream processing.

docs.title: Edge ordering
docs.text: Edges are stored as integer-ordered tuples: the smaller ASN always comes first. String ordering is not used — "22773" < "6" as strings but 22773 > 6 as integers.

docs.title: Justfile
docs.text:
The topology recipe runs build-topology.py three times (combined, v4, v6), passing both *.gz.* and *.bz2.* globs to merge RIS and RouteViews:

just date=20260101 topology

# Individual variants
just date=20260101 topology-combined
just date=20260101 topology-v4
just date=20260101 topology-v6

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Combined topology from a single date, RIS only
uv run build-topology.py \
  --input "./paths/20260101/*.gz.txt" \
  --output ./output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --filter-registered \
  --justify-output \
  --date 20260101

# Merge RIS and RouteViews
uv run build-topology.py \
  --input "./paths/20260101/*.gz.txt" \
  --input "./paths/20260101/*.bz2.txt" \
  --output ./output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --filter-registered \
  --justify-output \
  --date 20260101

# Also write the path list, use 8 workers
uv run build-topology.py \
  --input "./paths/20260101/*.gz.txt" \
  --output ./output/20260101/topology-20260101.txt \
  --paths \
  --workers 8
